newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles County takes budget to rating agencies.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles County takes budget to rating agencies.

text.p: Los Angeles County finance officials met Thursday with rating agencies in a bid to raise the county's credit standing.

The meetings with Standard & Poor's Corp, Moody's Investors Service Inc and Fitch Investors Service Inc in New York focused on the county's 1997-1998 budget proposal and its upcoming tax and revenue anticipation note (TRANs) sale, a county spokeswoman said.
"We're hoping to get a better rating (for the TRANs)," county spokeswoman Judy Hammond said.
Earlier this week, county supervisors approved a plan to issue up to $1.8 billion of TRANs for fiscal 1997-1998.
The note sale, which is expected to total $1.3 billion, would provide the county with the funds to meet its cash flow needs from July through December, the county said.
Pricing is expected in late June.
The supervisors are also finalizing the county's $11.97 billion budget proposal for 1997-1998. They will begin their final budget deliberations on June 23. The 1997-1998 fiscal year begins July 1.
